SR-001.justification: links() examines literal, subpath, class and glob targets in the parent (wired as the last step before the fork, macos/mod.rs:693, linux/mod.rs:859), applies the strict name count (src/audit.rs::a_hidden_file_needs_every_name_hidden) and Refuse yields HardLinks; escape_macos.rs and escape_linux.rs r08_* cover a protected alias (macOS, T1) and a hidden file aliased in a readable-only tree (all lanes). Gaps: AC3's second clause (a non-matching aliased file under a glob prefix is not a finding) contradicts the conservative may_overlap matching the updated statement prescribes, so the scenario needs reconciling in the model; and no test covers a secrets class file aliased outside every grant, a glob target, or hard links between unprotected files in a writable tree running without a finding (AC4).

SR-002.justification: Refuse is the default (macos/mod.rs:390, linux/mod.rs:508; default cages refused in the r08 canaries); Report runs and lists the file in Child::audit (r08_a_hard_link_to_a_hidden_file_is_refused); Off gives links_complete false (src/audit.rs::incomplete_is_never_clean_and_never_a_refusal); the receipt maps the mode and count, but no test checks the receipt of a Report or Off run (tests/audit.rs::the_receipt_counts_the_findings uses Refuse only).

SR-003.justification: A same-size rewrite with the modification time set back is Modified (change time in the key); a caged run's created .vscode/settings.json, modified .git/config, link with its target and nested .git are each counted exactly once; a quiet run is empty and complete. Passed locally on macOS; the integration tests are shared with Linux.

SR-004.justification: Both walks mark incomplete past the limit and on unreadable entries (src/audit.rs::walks_stay_put_and_say_what_they_could_not_read), an incomplete link check under Refuse lets the spawn run (incomplete_is_never_clean_and_never_a_refusal), and the receipt carries both completeness flags; but AC2 asks for the count the handoff audit reached and Audit has no handoff visited count (only links_visited), the receipt carries no visited count at all, and no test asserts links_visited or the receipt of an incomplete link check.

SR-005.justification: A tree holding a link loop and a link to the root is walked completely in under ten entries (the shared walker never follows links); the post-run snapshot lists a created link with its target read, not resolved (build -> /etc/passwd); walks descend only real directories on the root's device (audit.rs:372).

SR-006.justification: Child::audit (macOS child.rs:79, Linux child.rs:81) now ends the run with kill_all before the second walk, but ignores a kill_all failure and walks anyway; Child::receipt (macOS child.rs:88, Linux child.rs:90) calls finish, the second walk, without ending the run; the Audit has no incomplete-because-the-run-has-not-ended state, and neither acceptance scenario (a detached descendant still running, a Lifetime::Run descendant writing a hook after the child exits) is tested.

SR-007.justification: Findings hold PathBuf; receipt paths are ReceiptPath (text when valid UTF-8, else the bytes, untagged), which can round-trip; Display escapes control characters (newline tested in tests/audit.rs and src/audit.rs); no test serialises and reads back a name with an escape character or invalid UTF-8, or checks the bytes are equal.

SR-008.justification: before_spawn runs in the parent before command.spawn in both backends and RunAudit::finish runs from Child methods in the parent; no child-side code references the audit, and the multithreaded spawn test runs with the default link check.

SR-009.justification: The gate passes (run locally) and enforces non-ignored canaries per platform for R-08 (mitigated, six r08 canaries); R-07 stays harness/documented and says the audit lists findings for the harness to review; audits.md and the crate docs say an incomplete result is never clean and nowhere call an empty audit proof.

SR-010.justification: The same cage spawns cleanly, a second name is then given to a file under its protect subpath, and the next spawn is refused naming it; before_spawn re-walks the Targets on every spawn with no cached result (audit.rs:530).

SR-011.justification: On macOS and on every Linux tier a literal hide target that spawned cleanly is replaced by a symbolic link and the next spawn is refused with a symbolic finding; links() reads it with symlink_metadata and never follows it.

SR-012.justification: macOS asserts both link calls fail, and Linux now runs every tier with no skip and asserts the hidden-file link fails; but on T2 the protected-file attempt is neither made against a protected target nor asserted (the protect rule is added on T1 only, though T2 can protect a file outside the writable tree), so the T2 lane lacks the protected canary.

SR-013.justification: Without the policy the receipt JSON (policy and paths removed) holds no finding path and paths is None; with it paths is present; findings enter the summary only as counts (receipt.rs:443) and their paths only under the same gate.

SR-014.justification: Without with_handoff_audit no snapshot is taken and handoff is None; walk_limit defaults to 200,000 on both systems; the recorded latency probe puts the default link check within SC-003 on macOS and Linux T1/T2.

SR-015.justification: The refusal text lists two files each with its link count and names LinkAudit::Report and LinkAudit::Off; SpawnError's Display for HardLinks is that text on both systems (macos/mod.rs:326, linux/mod.rs:440) and carries every finding.
